subject: Staged commit smoothing and timing for reseller credit (ClearWave)
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearwave.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@clearwave.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Commit smoothing ask + reseller credit timing

Hi Hannah / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profiles for our inference workloads. We’re working through the procurement timeline and have a couple of asks that will influence our private-offer structure. High level:

- We prefer a phased commit (Q1 ramp -> Q2 baseline) instead of a single-year upfront commit. Can Redwood model a smoothing that preserves our price band while avoiding an immediate large spend?
- Related: our reseller (ClearWave’s channel partner) needs clarity on when reseller credits are triggered. For accounting we need an invoice-friendly cadence (quarterly crediting, ideally aligned with our true-ups).

Attached is a draft modeling sheet we ran on our side (simple MAPL bucket view) — can your team confirm whether the staged commit + quarterly reseller credit cadence is acceptable from a channel margin perspective? If so, we can proceed to a term sheet.

Thanks,
Emma Liu
Head of Cloud Procurement, ClearWave Analytics
[Attachment: clearwave_mapl_rebate_model.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38KB)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commit smoothing ask + reseller credit timing

Emma — thanks for the model and the clear asks. Quick responses below, then I’ll loop Ben and Camila for numbers and channel impact.

1) Staged commit: We can structure a two-phase commit (Q1 ramp to 60% of nominal, Q2 to 100%). That will allow ClearWave to capture a lower up-front cash swing while preserving list-equivalent unit pricing across the year.

2) Reseller credit timing: We can support quarterly reseller credits that reconcile to actual usage/true-ups. The main operational caveat is invoicing latency: credits applied on Redwood invoices will appear in the subsequent billing period. If ClearWave's channel partner needs same-period crediting, we’ll need a short funding holdback in the PO to match cashflows.

Ben/Camila — can you confirm the netback curve if we accept the staged commit and apply quarterly credits (no change to headline unit discount)? I’ve attached the model Emma sent and a sketch of the private-offer term sheet we’d propose.

Next steps: Ben to provide margin scenarios; Camila to confirm ops cadence for quarterly credits. If all aligned, we’ll produce a draft private-offer and route for signatures.

— Hannah
VP, Cloud GTM, Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: draft-private-offer-term-sheet.pdf (draft, 12 pages)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearwave.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commit smoothing ask + reseller credit timing

Hi all — ran three quick scenarios against the ClearWave MAPL file:

A) Front-loaded credit (standard 12-month) — list discount 18%, reseller credit applied at month-end, Redwood bears short-term margin pull forward. Effective Redwood gross margin impact: -5.2% over year.

B) Two-phase commit (Q1 60% -> Q2 100%), quarterly reseller credit with invoice-lag holdback (1 month) — headline discount unchanged, we amortize the credit to partner over next quarter. Gross margin impact: -2.1% over year.

C) Two-phase commit + small list protection (0.5% surcharge on overage) — reduces downside to -1.3% and keeps partner economics within their required floor.

Notes:
- Scenario B is our recommended compromise (lower immediate hit than A, partner gets predictable quarterly credits).
- Implementation ops: finance needs a short flag on the PO to indicate credit cadence; billing will auto-generate a reconciliation line tied to the deal id.

Attachments: I pushed a cleaned version of the MAPL with the margin waterfall to the drive link (see ticket). For quick visibility I’ve included the waterfall snapshot here: [Attachment: clearwave_mapl_rebate_model.xlsx (updated, 48KB)]

Camila — confirm whether Ops can accept the 1-month holdback on partner credits (so partner receives credits on their next invoice rather than same invoice).

Ben
Director, Marketplace Deals, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commit smoothing ask + reseller credit timing

Thanks — this is helpful. ClearWave procurement reviewed scenario B and can accept the 1-month holdback (quarterly crediting aligned to the next invoice). A couple of clarifications before we sign:

- Please add a short clause in the PO-term sheet that defines "reseller credit date" as the invoice cycle following the true-up quarter.
- We’d like a simple example row in the term sheet showing the cashflow for Q1/Q2 under the two-phase commit.

If you can incorporate those two items in the draft private-offer (and share an updated PDF), procurement will route for signature. We appreciate the flexibility here — this structure makes our CFO comfortable with cashflow timing while keeping unit economics stable.

Emma Liu
Head of Cloud Procurement, ClearWave Analytics
[Procurement contact: procurement@clearwave.com]
